evals.prompt: We're a skincare brand with 12k Instagram followers and a Klaviyo list. Goal is email subscribers. What should the entry methods be?
evals.expected_output: Email signup as the required action with opt-in wording and a stated entry weight. Two to four supporting actions on Instagram (follow, engage with a post) and a visit to a product page. A referral action, which can carry the highest weight of the list since it is optional and needs the incentive for reach. Leaves out account connections and content tasks. Cites the email family's uptake with n and labels it extracted. Ends with a next decision.
assertions: Email signup is required and given a stated entry weight
Mentions opt-in consent wording
Includes one sharing or referral action
Excludes app installs and account connections
Cites uptake figure with sample size and a source label in the reader's words (from Gleam campaign data, or the campaign count in brackets)
No platform pitch

evals.prompt: Here is my entry list: follow on X, follow on Instagram, follow on TikTok, join Discord, subscribe on YouTube, visit website, retweet, tag 3 friends, download our app, sign up to newsletter. All required. Is this good?
evals.expected_output: Flags too many required actions and channels the business may not run, recommends one asset-producing required action, moves app download and account-style actions to optional, keeps one sharing action, notes tag-a-friend rules vary by network, and says the data cannot show the effect of removing methods.
assertions: Recommends reducing required actions
Identifies the objective before ranking actions
Moves app download to optional
Mentions network rules for tag-a-friend
States the dataset cannot show the effect of method count

evals.prompt: Which entry method gets the most entries?
evals.expected_output: Explains that uptake describes completion when offered, names page visits and email signup as the highest-uptake families with figures and n, and redirects to the objective because high uptake on a visit produces nothing the business keeps.
assertions: Distinguishes uptake from value to the business
Cites the families with figures and sample sizes
Redirects to objective

evals.prompt: Style check applied to every conversational reply above.
evals.expected_output: Run the prize-picker evals/style_check.py on the saved reply. Zero em dashes, semicolons, curly quotes, assistant openers or closers.
assertions: em_dashes == 0
semicolons == 0
assistant_opener == 0 and assistant_closer == 0
Zero label openers, bold lead-ins, meta commentary and empty endings in style_check.py output
No mechanic is banned on the strength of an average, only on a rule, a law or a money risk

evals.prompt: We did not offer an Email Subscription Action, but have email addresses from User Details. Can we contact the Winner and add everyone to the newsletter? Does the subscription-Action benchmark show that most campaigns cannot contact anyone?
evals.expected_output: Checks available contact records for Winner administration and individual recorded marketing consent for the newsletter. Separates addresses, consent and subscription-Action usage. Explains consent via the User Details checkbox and explicit Newsletter signup without inferring permission from Action presence or absence.
assertions: Does not infer missing addresses from absence of a subscription Action
Uses available contact details for permitted Winner administration
Gates promotional messages on recorded marketing consent
Identifies both the User Details consent checkbox and explicit Newsletter signup
Does not turn Action usage or configuration rates into a consent or refusal rate

evals.prompt: We sell warehouse inventory software to operations managers. I would take 40 of the right people over 4,000 randoms from a giveaway. How do I set up entry so the wrong people stay out, and how will I know if it worked?
evals.expected_output: Names the buyer in one sentence and puts it in the title, first line and terms. Makes one qualifying question with answer choices the required action, takes the email from the entry form and leaves company, role and phone optional unless sales will use them. Sorts by answer and email domain after entry and treats a work-email requirement as a decision that turns away some real buyers, with no split of work against free mail quoted. Names who contacts each tier and how fast. Replaces Entrants and Conversion Rate with qualified Entrants, cost per qualified Entrant, replies, meetings and pipeline. Says the B2B figures show what businesses chose and end at the entry, that 40 Entrants is below the 100-Entrant floor of the data, and labels the gating, question and follow-up advice as practice.
assertions: Gives a one-sentence buyer definition and says where to put it in the campaign
Makes one qualifying question the required action, with answer choices, and says nobody is rejected on the answer
Offers sorting by email domain after entry as the default and says a work-email requirement turns away some real buyers
States that no work-email against free-mail split exists in the data and quotes none
Names an owner and a response time for each tier and labels the time as judgement
Replaces crowd measures with qualified Entrants, cost per qualified Entrant and pipeline, and says the crowd benchmarks can be ignored
Says the B2B figures describe what businesses chose, end at the entry and cannot show lead quality
Labels gating, the qualifying question and follow-up as practice, with no causal claim

evals.prompt: We're a healthcare SaaS in the US selling to clinic managers. Legal won't let us do anything that looks like we're paying for a review or a referral, and we can't collect anything that could be PHI. We want qualified demo requests out of this, not a list of randoms. Nobody on the team can moderate a Discord. What do people actually do to enter?
evals.expected_output: Drops referral, review and Discord actions and says what each drop costs. Makes the required action a qualifying question about the clinic's workflow with answer choices and no patient or personal health detail, plus a visit to the pricing or product page. Takes the email from the entry form with marketing permission as a separate tick. Says the pairing of question and email is the skill's own advice with no measured result, and that the B2B data holds what businesses chose and ends at the entry.
assertions: Leaves out referral, review and Discord actions and says why
The qualifying question asks about the clinic and never asks for patient or health data
Keeps marketing permission separate from entry consent
Labels the question and follow-up as practice with no dataset support
States that the data cannot show lead quality
